source.title: Towards Sample-efficient Overparameterized Meta-learning
source.authors: Yue Sun; Adhyyan Narang; Halil Ibrahim Gulluk; Samet Oymak; Maryam Fazel

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test-risk curves as representation dimension changes, using frozen pretrained features and linear-regression meta-learning rather than the original deep-network size sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own representation-dimension sweeps in Figures 1, 3, and 5; those are included. Results it cites from other work, including prior double-descent findings, are not rows. Covariance-alignment and sample-complexity results do not measure test error against representation dimension and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own few-shot test-error curves as representation dimension R crosses the interpolation point R=n2. It does this in a new setting: transfer and meta-learning with a linear head on frozen ResNet-50 features, and min-norm linear regression. These results bear on the general (V4) double-descent curve. They do not bear on model-wise double descent in deep networks, because no network is resized.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude the optimal linear representation is typically overparameterized and beats subspace (projection) representations when eigen-weighted. They also find that feature-task covariance alignment lowers sample complexity. Finally, limited representation-learning data creates a tradeoff favouring smaller R. They frame Fig 1(a) as double descent in transfer learning.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than sweeping the size of a deep network in standard supervised training, the study varies the dimension of frozen pretrained features or linear meta-learning representations and measures few-shot error; it also compares eigen-weighted and unweighted representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with few-shot training size n2, task-covariance spikedness ι, eigen-weighting, and prior-task sample count n1.

fits_no_version.finding: In the overparameterized regime, optimal eigen-weighting gives lower few-shot error than an unweighted projection. Weighting has no effect when underparameterized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of the second descent depends on an inductive-bias weighting (a weighted ridge prior) in the interpolator.

record.peer_reviewed: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021), Sydney, Australia
record.problems: The main test-error curves are plots without stated numerical values or uncertainty bars. The empirical deep-feature experiment uses a frozen pretrained ResNet-50 and varies representation dimension rather than deep-network size; the linear experiments are specialized meta-learning settings.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying test-error-versus-dimension findings were left out. Cited findings from other studies and the paper's covariance-alignment, estimator-error, and sample-complexity results were excluded because they do not report the claimed test-error curve.

untested.parts: No deep network is resized. The only network (ResNet-50) is frozen, and only the linear head's feature count R varies.
No sweep over epochs or training time.
Curves are shown at several n2 values, but there is no claim or analysis that more samples raise error near the threshold.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location.
Eigen-weighting, a ridge-type prior per Observation 1, lowers overparameterized error. Whether it removes the peak is not stated. Label noise and multiple descent are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 links are moved to V4, because no deep network is resized; the deep-network evidence is a frozen ResNet-50 with only the linear head's feature count R varied. Neither original source (1912.02292, 1812.11118) is this study. All curve rows are figure-only with no numbers. Figs 3 and 5 plot theoretical risk.

versions.untested_parts: It varies feature-representation dimension, not the size of a deep network itself; the ResNet experiment freezes all but the final layer.
No test-error sweep over training epochs or time.
Although curves are shown for different few-shot training sizes, the study does not report that increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
The reported general-model-class evidence is from linear-regression meta-learning; it does not establish the curve across multiple model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
No test of label-noise-driven peaks, multiple or triple descent, or disappearance of the peak under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective parameter measure to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relationships.condition: Frozen ResNet-50 features with a linear head on CIFAR-10, and synthetic min-norm linear regression with optimal eigen-weighting or perfect covariance
relationships.reason: Error falls again once R exceeds n2 in the transfer experiment (r1-r3). In the weighted linear setting, the overparameterized error is below the underparameterized error, and the peak is at R=n2 (r4, r6, r8, r10, r12, r17).
relationships.display_finding: Transfer error declined once R exceeded n2, while weighted linear regression peaked at R=n2 and achieved lower error beyond interpolation than below it.

relationships.condition: Representation estimated from a finite number of prior-task samples
relationships.reason: The authors report a sweet spot: estimation error grows with R, so further overparameterization stops helping when representation learning is inaccurate (r14-r16).
